events.title: First Pony Express Ride Begins
events.description: The first riders of the Pony Express departed from St. Joseph, Missouri, and Sacramento, California, carrying mail across roughly 1,900 miles of the American West in about ten days.
events.significance: The Pony Express dramatically shortened mail delivery times between the East and the West Coast and became a lasting symbol of the American frontier, though it was made obsolete by the transcontinental telegraph in October 1861.

events.title: Truman Signs the Marshall Plan into Law
events.description: U.S. President Harry S. Truman signed the Economic Cooperation Act, authorizing the European Recovery Program, known as the Marshall Plan, to provide billions of dollars in aid to rebuild Western Europe after World War II.
events.significance: The plan helped revive war-torn European economies, strengthened democratic institutions, and countered the spread of communism, shaping the postwar order and laying groundwork for European cooperation.

events.title: Martin Luther King Jr. Delivers the 'I've Been to the Mountaintop' Speech
events.description: On the eve of his assassination, Martin Luther King Jr. gave his final speech at Mason Temple in Memphis, Tennessee, in support of striking sanitation workers.
events.significance: The speech is regarded as one of the most powerful and prophetic addresses of the civil rights movement, and it became a poignant final statement of King's legacy of nonviolent activism and economic justice.

events.title: First Handheld Cellular Phone Call Is Made
events.description: Martin Cooper, a Motorola engineer, made the first public call on a handheld portable cellular phone in New York City, reportedly calling a rival at Bell Labs.
events.significance: This call marked the birth of mobile telephony, paving the way for the global mobile communications revolution and the smartphones that define modern life.

events.title: Outlaw Jesse James Is Shot and Killed
events.description: Jesse James was shot dead by Robert Ford, a member of his own gang, at his home in St. Joseph, Missouri, for the reward offered by the governor.
events.significance: His death ended one of the most notorious outlaw careers in American history and cemented James's status as a legendary figure of the Old West.
